newsitem.title: INDIA: More than 1,000 Indian deportees arrive from Saudi.
newsitem.headline: More than 1,000 Indian deportees arrive from Saudi.

text.p: More than 1,000 Indians deported by Saudi Arabia for not having valid travel documents, returned home by ship in India's commercial capital of Bombay on Monday, police and officials said.
There were six women and 21 beggar children among the 1,182 people aboard the "Al-Madina" which docked in Bombay after a six-day journey from Jeddah, port authorities told Reuters.
"The vessel earlier called at Karachi, and about 900 Pakistanis were put ashore there," one official said.
Authorities said the deportees were expelled following a vigorous campaign against illegal migrants that began in the Gulf countries late last year.

Many had gone to jobs in the Gulf, but others said they went on the Haj pilgrimage when hundreds of thousands of faithful gather in the holy city of Mecca, only to be stranded there after losing their passports.
"I went for the Haj with my father in January, and we got separated," said eight-year-old Nadeem, who hails from Murshidabad in India's eastern state of West Bengal.

"My father went out of the house one day and didn't come back," he said. Nadeem believes his father lost his passport and was jailed by the police. Later, he himself was picked up by police as he wandered the streets and spent a few days in jail.
Fulrunissa, a purdah-clad Moslem woman from the southern Indian state of Tamil Nadu, who appeared to be in her thirties, said she went to Saudi Arabia as a maidservant.
"But it was a huge house with seven children and lots of work. I wasn't able to manage. My employers beat me and tortured me repeatedly," she said tearfully.
"Finally one night, I ran away and went to the police station, but the police advised me to return to my job."
Fulrunissa said she refused to do this, and stayed at the police station until she was finally deported to India.
"I went there on a job," said Abdullah Mohammed, 35. "I worked for six or seven months, but I didn't like the work and I got fed up. I let the police arrest me."
But Mohammed said his experience had not discouraged him and he planned to return again soon.
"I will stay in India for three or four months and then go back on another job," he added.
Police officials said the children would be held at a remand home in Bombay until arrangements could be made for their return to their home state of West Bengal.
"Once we have verified that all the other passengers are in fact Indian, they too will be allowed to go home," a police officer said. "But since they've been sent here, that should not be a problem."
Gulf countries have in that last few months deported tens of thousands of migrant workers, mostly from India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka and the Philippines.
